prompt: Act as a professional career coach and technical resume writer. TASK: Analyze the job description provided below to extract the essential technical keywords, tools, and professional competencies the hirer is seeking. Prioritize skills and tools listed as required or core responsibilities over those listed as nice to have or bonus. If the job description names specific tools or platforms by name, prioritize including those exact names in the tech stack over generic or secondary tools. When the job description lists multiple interchangeable or equivalent tools for the same purpose (for example several AI assistants, cloud providers, or databases presented as alternatives), prefer whichever option the applicant's CV shows genuine experience with, rather than defaulting to the first one listed or the most popular one. Also identify which single soft skill or behavioral trait the job description emphasizes most, such as independent ownership, cross functional collaboration, client communication, mentorship, or adaptability. You will also be given the applicant's current CV as additional context. Based on the job requirements and the applicant's real background, design one representative project entry for the applicant's CV that demonstrates expertise in the core skills the hirer wants, while remaining plausible given the applicant's actual experience level and skillset. FRAMING: Treat this project as something the applicant built independently to demonstrate their own ability (a self-directed, personal, or portfolio-style project), not as a system that was adopted, deployed to production, or put into use by an employer, team, or organization. Do not use phrasing that implies institutional adoption or real-world operational use, even implicitly (avoid constructions like 'helped the organization', 'the company adopted', 'the team relied on', 'deployed to production', 'used by stakeholders', or similar). At the same time, do not explicitly label the project as a 'demo', 'prototype', 'proof of concept', or 'learning project' either; simply describe what the system does, how it was built, and its intended purpose in a way that is neither corporate-adoption language nor self-deprecating. REQUIREMENTS: Use professional, high-impact, persuasive language. The project name must be a maximum of 4 words, short and punchy, clear and unambiguous about what the project actually does, no subtitle or colon. The tech stack must list a maximum of 4 technologies, comma-separated, weighted toward the job description's required or core tools rather than its nice-to-have tools, and every technology listed must be explicitly referenced or clearly implied within the bullets, do not include a technology in the tech stack that the bullets never use. Only use technologies, tools, platforms, APIs, or services that have a genuine free plan, free tier, or can be used entirely for free. Do not include any tool that requires a paid subscription with no free plan or free tier, even if it appears in the job description. When multiple equivalent tools satisfy the same requirement, always prefer the free option that best matches the applicant's CV. Write exactly 2 bullet points, each 1-2 lines, technically specific, and results-oriented. At least one bullet should subtly demonstrate the soft skill or behavioral trait identified above through the work described, without stating it directly as an adjective or trait name. At least one bullet should briefly convey the practical purpose or intended use of the project in plain language, such as what problem it solves or what it is designed to help with, without using numbers, percentages, or quantified metrics, and without asserting that it was adopted, deployed, or used by an organization or team. Do not use em dashes anywhere in the output, use commas, periods, or parentheses instead. Maintain internal coherence: the project name, tech stack, and bullets must all describe ONE plausible, believable project, not a generic list of buzzwords. Do not fabricate implausible achievements, keep claims realistic for an individual contributor working on their own initiative, and stay consistent with the applicant's CV where relevant. OUTPUT FORMAT: Return ONLY a raw, valid JSON object, no preamble, no markdown code fences, no explanation, no trailing text. It must match this exact schema: {"project_name": "string (max 4 words, clear and unambiguous)", "tech_stack": "string (comma-separated, max 4 technologies, all referenced in the bullets, prioritizing required tools from the job description and matching the applicant's CV when alternatives exist)", "bullets": ["string (bullet 1)", "string (bullet 2)"]}.
